title: IEC 61000-6-1 EMC Immunity Testing Lab
description: IEC 61000-6-1:2016 EMC immunity testing in India for residential, commercial and light-industrial equipment, covering ESD, RF, surge and EFT with ITC India.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Electrical and electronic equipment is routinely exposed to electromagnetic disturbances generated by electrostatic discharge, switching devices, radio-frequency transmitters, power networks and other electrical equipment. EMC immunity testing helps determine whether a product can continue to operate acceptably when exposed to these disturbances.
ITC India provides IEC 61000-6-1 EMC immunity testing for applicable electrical and electronic equipment intended for residential, commercial, public and light-industrial environments.

IEC 61000-6-1 is a generic immunity standard. It is generally applicable where no dedicated product or product-family EMC immunity standard exists. Manufacturers should therefore identify the correct product standard before selecting IEC 61000-6-1 as the compliance route.
For broader electromagnetic compatibility requirements, manufacturers can also review ITC India’s EMC Testing Laboratory services.

sections.heading: What Is IEC 61000-6-1?
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-1:2016, Edition 3.0 specifies generic EMC immunity requirements for electrical and electronic equipment intended for use in residential, commercial, public and light-industrial locations.
The standard covers immunity requirements relating to continuous and transient, conducted and radiated electromagnetic disturbances, including electrostatic discharge.

The standard applies to relevant equipment used indoors or outdoors in these environments and can also apply to battery-powered equipment or equipment powered by non-industrial low-voltage distribution systems.
However, IEC 61000-6-1 should normally be used only when a more specific product or product-family immunity standard is not available.

sections.heading: ESD, RF and Transient Immunity Testing
paragraphs: Electrostatic discharge can occur when a user or nearby object transfers accumulated static charge to the equipment. IEC 61000-4-2 testing evaluates whether the product can tolerate applicable contact and air discharge conditions without unacceptable degradation.
Radiated RF immunity evaluates equipment while it is exposed to electromagnetic fields. Conducted RF testing examines disturbances coupled onto applicable cables and ports.

EFT and surge testing simulate transient disturbances that can occur due to switching operations and power-network events. These tests are particularly important for equipment connected to mains power or external signal and control cables.

sections.heading: EMC Immunity and EMC Emissions Are Different
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-1 addresses immunity—the ability of equipment to operate satisfactorily when electromagnetic disturbances are present.
It does not serve as the generic emissions standard for the same environment.

Where a generic emissions standard is applicable, manufacturers should also review IEC 61000-6-3 EMC emissions testing. IEC 61000-6-3 addresses emission requirements for equipment used in residential environments and related locations.
Considering immunity and emissions together helps manufacturers develop a more complete EMC compliance strategy.

sections.heading: Performance Criteria During Immunity Testing
paragraphs: A product does not necessarily have to operate identically during every electromagnetic disturbance. The relevant performance criteria define what level of degradation, interruption or temporary loss of function may be acceptable during or after a particular test.

sections.heading: Preparing Equipment for IEC 61000-6-1 Testing
paragraphs: Manufacturers should provide representative samples together with sufficient technical documentation.

Useful information includes the product specification, intended environment, AC or DC input ratings, I/O ports, cable types and lengths, normal operating modes, accessories, external power supplies, user instructions and any previous EMC test results.
Early EMC evaluation can also help identify weaknesses associated with PCB layout, grounding, cable routing, shielding, filtering or enclosure design before final compliance testing.

sections.heading: IEC 61000-6-1 Testing Support from ITC India
paragraphs: ITC India supports electrical and electronic product manufacturers with electromagnetic compatibility testing against applicable IEC and international EMC requirements.
A test program can be planned according to the product’s intended environment, available product-specific standards, applicable ports and required immunity phenomena.
To discuss IEC 61000-6-1 applicability and the required EMC test configuration for your product, submit your technical details through the ITC India testing and certification inquiry.

sections.heading: What is IEC 61000-6-1?
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-1 is a generic EMC immunity standard for electrical and electronic equipment intended for residential, commercial, public and light-industrial environments.

sections.heading: What is the current edition of IEC 61000-6-1?
paragraphs: The current IEC publication is IEC 61000-6-1:2016, Edition 3.0.

sections.heading: When should IEC 61000-6-1 be used?
paragraphs: It is generally used when the equipment falls within its environmental scope and no relevant dedicated product or product-family EMC immunity standard exists.

sections.heading: What tests are included in IEC 61000-6-1?
paragraphs: Applicable testing can include ESD, radiated RF immunity, conducted RF immunity, EFT/burst, surge, magnetic-field immunity and voltage dips or short interruptions.

sections.heading: What is the difference between IEC 61000-6-1 and IEC 61000-6-3?
paragraphs: IEC 61000-6-1 addresses electromagnetic immunity, while IEC 61000-6-3 addresses electromagnetic emissions for applicable equipment and environments.

sections.heading: Does every product require all IEC 61000-6-1 immunity tests?
paragraphs: No. The applicable tests depend on the equipment configuration, ports, power supply and intended operating conditions.
